evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: This call will just take around ten to fifteen minutes then I will be able to build you an accurate code you can depend on. Is now a good time? [customer confirms yes]
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: I'd like to ask first what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about two-move scenario (apartment → storage → apartment) and pricing worry. Rep follows up: 'Yeah, we can definitely do that. We actually have done that many times before...' and 'For your first move you'd like it to be done tomorrow. Is that right?' This is genuine follow-up that unpacks the underlying issue.

top_strength: Nicole gathered comprehensive logistics details upfront (property type, floor, dimensions, special items, storage location) and asked the customer's biggest concerns before diving into logistics, which allowed her to tailor the conversation to a two-move scenario the customer needed.
coaching_note: After presenting the estimate, ask 'Does that feel fair?' and hold genuine silence for the customer to respond—this was skipped entirely, and Section 6's final concerns check was a perfunctory 'Do you have any questions?' rather than a genuine *'What's still concerning you about this move?'* that would surface real objections.
